title: Create listing form and listings page

history.detail:
FAIL: QA1 gate-1 static audit, sprint 1, commit 36f7af0. VERDICT: FAIL.

Sprint file re-read fresh from docs/sprints/2-in-progress/ immediately before this verdict, not from an earlier read in this session. No version-pair acceptance criterion exists in this sprint (the file explicitly rules out any publish or version bump), so the "does the file actually differ between A and B" check does not apply. Working tree clean; HEAD is 36f7af0, so what I audited is committed.

One blocking defect. Everything else in this sprint is met, and met well - the FAIL is not a judgement on the app code, which is good. Details below, blocker first.

BLOCKER - the scaffold bricks this repository's own lifecycle tooling

package.json:5 adds "type": "module" at the repository root. This repo's framework scripts are CommonJS, and Node resolves a .js file's module type from the nearest package.json walking up. Before this commit there was no package.json at the root at all (git show d096a37:package.json - "exists on disk, but not in d096a37"), so those scripts loaded as CommonJS. As of 36f7af0 every one of them fails to load.

Demonstrated, not argued. Every invocation below is from this checkout at 36f7af0:

  node scripts/run-lifecycle.js qa1 1 --verdict PASS --notes-file qa1-notes-1.txt
    ReferenceError: require is not defined in ES module scope
    at scripts/run-lifecycle.js:25 - "This file is being treated as an ES module
    because it has a '.js' file extension and package.json contains type: module"

  node scripts/run-lifecycle.js status 1     -> same ReferenceError
  node scripts/launcher/run-role.js --help   -> same ReferenceError
  node scripts/mc-commit.js                  -> same ReferenceError

Control, to show the breakage is the module type and not something else:
  python3 scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py status 1   -> works, prints sprint 1 at dev_build

Scope. 15 CommonJS files are affected - scripts/install.js, scripts/mc-commit.js, scripts/run-lifecycle.js, and 12 files under scripts/launcher/ (agents, auth, claude-cmd, content-hash, generate-tasks, jsonc, prompts, python-interpreter, rel-path-key, role-claims, run-role, session). All 14 sprint-* slash commands invoke "node scripts/..." and therefore all 14 are dead: sprint-new, sprint-start, sprint-status, sprint-list, sprint-qa1, sprint-dev-done, sprint-ship, sprint-reship, sprint-repoint, sprint-liveqa, sprint-complete, sprint-abort, sprint-block, sprint-rename. That is every role's entire command surface, not just mine. I could not record this verdict through the documented path and had to fall back to the Python entry point directly.

Why this is a FAIL and not a note. Req 1 asked for a Vite + React + TS scaffold in this repository's root, and the standard scaffold ships type:module, so this is an honest collision rather than carelessness. But "npm run build/test/lint pass" is not the same fact as "the repository still works," and the second one is what actually matters here. The sprint file did not anticipate the collision either - worth Master Controller's attention when planning sprint 2 - but it needs no amendment, because this is fixable in the app's own files.

Two fixes, both verified mechanically in a throwaway repro outside this repo (root package.json with type:module + a CJS file under scripts/ reproduces the exact ReferenceError; each fix below then makes it print normally). Dev Team picks one and verifies it against the real scripts - I am naming the constraint, not writing the change:

  a) Drop "type": "module" from the root package.json. The app is .ts/.tsx compiled by Vite and vite.config.ts is loaded by Vite's own loader, so the app should not care - but confirm dev, build, preview and test all still pass, since this is the one that touches the app's own module semantics.
  b) Add scripts/package.json containing {"type":"commonjs"}. Stops Node's upward walk at scripts/ and leaves the app as ESM. Touches no framework file's contents.

Whichever you pick, the check that matters is that "node scripts/run-lifecycle.js status 1" prints sprint status instead of a stack trace, plus npm run build and npm test still clean. Re-run /sprint-qa1 when it is committed.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE - all 10 met on their own terms

Req 1 scaffold - MET as specified, but see the blocker: the scaffold satisfies its stated criteria and still breaks the repo. Scripts dev/build/preview/lint/test all exist. I ran them rather than taking the handoff's word: npm run build exits 0 (tsc -b + vite build, 31 modules, dist emitted), npm test exits 0 (5 files, 13 tests), npm run lint exits 0. No Vite boilerplate: grepped 36f7af0 for vite.svg, react.svg, "count is", useState(0), read-the-docs, App.css - zero hits outside package-lock. No src/assets. public/ holds only a hand-written favicon.svg. src/index.css is hand-written, not Vite's default.

Req 2 Listing type - MET. src/types/listing.ts, one shared module, exactly the nine named fields and no others. price typed string with the comment explaining why it stays a string. id from crypto.randomUUID() in the provider, never array position. NewListingInput is Omit<Listing,'id'> in the same module - derived, not a second definition of the shape. Correct call.

Req 3 in-memory store - MET. git grep over src/ + index.html + vite.config.ts at 36f7af0 for localStorage, sessionStorage, indexedDB, fetch(, axios returns exactly one hit: the comment in ListingsProvider.tsx disclaiming them. React useState in a provider, useCallback and useMemo around the value.

Req 4 client-side routing, store above router - MET, checked explicitly rather than assumed, as the criterion demands. main.tsx nests ListingsProvider > BrowserRouter > App, so no route change can unmount the provider. Zero raw anchor tags in src, zero window.location, zero alert(. preventDefault at CreateListingPage.tsx:59, plus noValidate so native validation does not pre-empt the inline errors. src/test/renderApp.tsx mirrors the same nesting, so page tests exercise the real wiring.

Req 5 create form - MET. Eight fields, each labelled and bound by htmlFor/id. Both dates are type="date". Tips carry the section-6 category labels (food/coffee, activity/place, neighbourhood), not Tip 1/2/3. Single Post Listing submit.

Req 6 validation - MET. validate() at CreateListingPage.tsx:22 requires title, neighbourhood, price (trimmed, so whitespace-only fails) and both dates. Date order compares ISO strings, which is correct for YYYY-MM-DD, and permits equal dates - right reading of "must not be earlier than". Tips explicitly unvalidated, with a comment saying why. Errors render in-page with role="alert". No alert() in the diff.

Req 7 submit adds and lands on listings - MET. addListing then navigate('/listings'), client-side.

Req 8 listings page and click target - MET. Each row renders exactly the four named fields. The row is a Link, so a real anchor: tab-reachable and Enter-activatable with no custom key handling. /listings/:id resolves to ListingDetailPlaceholder, a deliberate stub.

Req 9 empty state - MET. Explicit listings.length === 0 branch, "No listings yet." plus a Link to /create.

Req 10 date helper - MET. src/utils/formatDate.ts is the single helper, format documented ("Jan 5, 2026", Intl dateStyle medium), used at every date render site in the diff. The UTC-midnight parse is a deliberate fix for the local-timezone day-shift bug and the test covers the boundary.

CODE QUALITY

Test coverage: real, not decorative. 13 tests, 5 files. App.test.tsx exercises Req 4's actual risk - post, navigate create to listings to create, listing survives. ListingsPage.test.tsx asserts the row href matches /listings/.+ and that clicking lands on the non-404 placeholder. CreateListingPage.test.tsx asserts the rendered error strings themselves, which is what the criterion asks for. Zero-tips post is covered - the requirement most likely to get broken later by someone tidying validation. The afterEach(cleanup) in src/test/setup.ts was found and fixed during self-verify rather than handed to me as a flaky suite. Right order of operations.

Error handling: nothing swallowed. The only throw is useListings outside its provider, a genuine programmer error, and it is tested. No empty catch blocks in src.

Standards compliance: shared types used properly, never redefined locally. The three-file store split exists to satisfy oxlint's only-export-components rule, not architecture theatre. Neither over- nor under-engineered for a prototype.

Security: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, no eval, no network, no user input reaching a URL except a generated UUID in a route path. React escapes rendered text. No injection or XSS surface.

OTHER ISSUES - low severity, none blocking, fix alongside the blocker or leave for later

1. LOW - src/utils/formatDate.ts:20. Throws RangeError: Invalid time value on an empty or malformed date string. Verified against "", "not-a-date", "2026-13-45" - all three throw. Not reachable this sprint: validation guarantees both dates non-empty and the form's date inputs are the only way into the store. Flagging it because Req 10 hands this helper to sprint 2, which will feed it values derived from a route param.

2. LOW - package.json:9. npm run lint runs oxlint across the whole repo, so it lints the framework's scripts/ and emits 11 no-unused-vars warnings from scripts/launcher/role-claims.js and scripts/mc-commit.js - files this app does not own. Exit 0, so Req 1's "lint must pass" is genuinely satisfied. The cost is that a real future warning in src/ arrives buried in noise. An ignorePatterns entry for scripts/ fixes it.

3. LOW - src/pages/CreateListingPage.test.tsx:56. The empty-title test asserts the error text and that we stayed on the create screen, but never asserts the store is still empty. A regression that added the listing AND blocked navigation would pass. Criterion is met as written; this is test strength, not a gap against Req 6.

4. LOW - src/pages/CreateListingPage.tsx. Errors persist after the user corrects the field, until the next submit, and inputs are not tied to their error text via aria-describedby or aria-invalid. Not required by any requirement here. Polish sprint.

RECOMMENDATION

Back to dev_build. Fix the root module-type collision so "node scripts/run-lifecycle.js status 1" runs, keep npm run build and npm test clean, commit, and re-run /sprint-qa1 for a fresh gate-1 audit. Nothing ships until that passes - and note that until it is fixed, Pipeman cannot run /sprint-ship and Dev Team cannot run /sprint-dev-done anyway, because those commands are themselves broken by this defect.

The app code is in good shape. Fix the one thing.
